blocks.title: Evaluation depends on batch size with frozen weights
blocks.why: the weights are identical in every cell; only the number of samples per forward pass changes, so a published IoU on this benchmark is not defined without its evaluation batch size

blocks.title: Released baselines that never predict the positive class
blocks.as_published: reported as crop-type baselines, with a macro IoU
blocks.as_measured: [L8]_utae: macro IoU 0.3812 but paddy IoU 0.0000 and non-paddy recall 1.000; [S2]_utae: macro IoU 0.3812 but paddy IoU 0.0000 and non-paddy recall 1.000
blocks.why: a model that labels every pixel non-paddy still earns a macro IoU near 0.38 from the negative class alone, so the headline metric does not reveal that the model has learned nothing about paddy

blocks.title: The phenology column labelled MAPE is MAE / 183
blocks.as_measured: val_mae / 183 = 17.1828 / 183 = 0.093895; matches for 24 of 24 released phenology runs, worst disagreement 1.05e-08
blocks.why: 183 is a constant, not each field's true day, so the column is a rescaled MAE and not a percentage error. The dataset paper defines it this way; the released logs do not, which is where the misreading comes from. This is reported as a metric that invites misreading, not as a defect in the benchmark's definition

blocks.title: Every released yield model has a higher MAE than a constant
blocks.as_published: 24 released yield checkpoints, reported with MAE, RMSE and MAPE, with no constant baseline in the benchmark
blocks.as_measured: constant = training-split mean = 1841.9 kg/acre, MAE 435.9; best checkpoint [S2]_utae MAE 497.0; 24 of 24 checkpoints worse than the constant
blocks.why: the comparison is on the same 41 validation field-seasons and the same ground truth the gate uses; the constant uses no imagery at all

scope: reads cached evaluation artefacts; does not re-execute any model
